How many ticks between Bouncer shoves.
60 ticks = 1 second
Reducing this value can dramatically overpower Bouncer.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_BouncerDistance_toolt:
The distance (in tile squares) from the player out to which Bouncer begins attempting to shove enemies away.
Lower values means Bouncer will take effect only at closer ranges to the player.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_BouncerEffectiveness_:
The percent chance that a player who has the Bouncer trait will trigger its effect.
This is rolled every tick, so 60 times/second for as long as the player has at least two or more zombies near them.
Increasing this value by even a small amount can dramatically overpower Bouncer.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_BurnedDistance_toolti:
Distance at which Burn Ward Patient gets activated by fire.
Keep in mind, the higher this value is, the more panic and anxiety you will get from being close.

Sandbox_MoreTraits_BurnedPanic_tooltip:
Panic you will get from Burn Ward Patient.
Scaling works by repeatedly adding panic until max distance number is reached, starting from distance of closest fire.
What this means is, if fire is 1 tile away and max is 20, it will give 20x panic than this number. This happens every one minute in-game.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_BurnedStress_tooltip:
Stress you will get from Burn Ward Patient.
Scaling works by repeatedly adding stress until max distance number is reached, starting from distance of closest fire.
What this means is, if fire is 1 tile away and max is 20, it will give 20x stress than this number. This happens every one minute in-game.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_ButterfingersChance_t:
The chance in X how frequently a player with Butterfingers will drop an item.
The base chance is 5, so by default this value would be a 5/2000 chance calculated every in-game minute.
Lowering this value could result in players constantly dropping their items.

Sandbox_MoreTraits_GymGoerNoExerciseFati:
Should Gym Goer affect Exercise Fatigue?

Sandbox_MoreTraits_HardyEndurance_toolti: How much extra endurance should hardy give?
Sandbox_MoreTraits_HoarderCompatibility_:
If you run both More Traits and Expended Traits, they both have perks that update carry weight.
If this is checked on, Hoarder (from Expended Traits) and carry weight from this mod (Pack Mule/Mouse) will stack. Which means that whatever carry weight you get with Pack Mule/Pack Mouse will be multiplied by 1.25.
If this is checked off, and you have both perks (Hoarder and Pack Mule/Mouse) either Hoarder or Pack Mouse/Mule will run its code first meaing I honestly don't know if your max weight will be calculated by Hoarder code or Pack Mule code

Sandbox_MoreTraits_IncomprehensiveChance:

After how many in-game days should the indefatigable ability recharge?

What percent of unknown recipes should be learned by Ingenuitive?

Sandbox_MoreTraits_IngenuitiveLimit_tool:
Limit the amount of free recipes granted by Ingenuitive?

Sandbox_MoreTraits_QuickWorkerScaler_too:
Determines how much faster players with the Quick Worker trait perform actions.
Set this to 50 for a 50% reduction in time (twice as fast).
Set to 10 for a 10% reduction.
Default: 50.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_ScroungerChance_toolt:
A percent value representing the chance that a player with the Scrounger trait will find extra loot in any container.
100% would make every container have extra loot.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_ScroungerItemChance_t:
A percent value representing how likely any item in a container is to be duplicated by Scrounger.
For example: Scrounger Chance is the percent chance that any given container will potentially have extra loot in it.
Once a container passes this initial check, another series of checks is run - for every single item inside that container, a die is rolled to determine if that item is duplicated.
If for instance, this value is set to 100%, then whenever Scrounger is triggered, the entire contents of that container will be duplicated.
If Scrounger Chance, and Scrounger Item Chance are both 100%, then anyone with the Scrounger trait will find double the loot in every container.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_ScroungerLootModifier:
A percent value representing how much extra loot players with the Scrounger trait will find when Scrounger triggers.
100% would double the amount of extra loot players find.
This value always rounds up, so even a single item can potentially be doubled.
This effect is most noticed in stacks of items such as cigarettes or ammunition.
Sandbox_MoreTraits_SecondWindCooldown_to: After how much days should Second Wind recharge?
Sandbox_MoreTraits_SlowWorkerScaler_tool:
Determines how much slower players with the Slow Worker trait perform actions.
Set this to 50 for a 50% increase in time (1.5x longer).

Sandbox_MoreTraits_SuperImmuneFirstInfec: Super Immune Less Time After Curing

Sandbox_MoreTraits_UnwaveringDamageBoost:
Determines the damage boost received when certain conditions are met. Damage scales based on the following:

Tier 1 (Default 2.0x): Endurance < 25%, Fatigue > 80%, or Pain > 75.
Tier 2 (Default 1.5x): Endurance < 50%, Fatigue > 70%, or Pain > 50.
Tier 3 (Default 1.25x): Endurance < 75%, Fatigue > 60%, or Pain > 20.

If multiple conditions are met, only the highest tier applies.

Sandbox_SkillRecoveryJournalModDataTrack:
USE WITH CAUTION.

Example syntax: ModDataKey1|ModDataKey2
Transcription will store a copy of the corresponding table from the player's mod data. 
This can create significant issues if the data is large.
 If you're not sure what any of this means, ignore it, and leave blank.

Sandbox_ETW_AffinitySystemGainMultiplier: How much easier it is to gain perks that have Affinity System functionality (only affects perks you started with!). Setting it to 1 would mean that it doesn't make it easier to gain. Setting it to 2 means it'll take twice as fast to gain them. Setting it to 1.5 would make it 50% faster, and so on. So if you start with a positive dynamic trait and later lose it, you'll get it back much faster. But it also affects negative traits!
Sandbox_ETW_AffinitySystemLoseDivider_to: How much harder it is to lose perks that have Affinity System functionality (only affects perks you started with!). Setting it to 1 would mean that it doesn't make it harder to lose. Setting it to 2 means you'll be twice as slow to lose them. Setting it to 1.5 would make it 50% slower, and so on. So if you start with a positive trait that you can lose, it'll be much harder to lose it. But it also affects negative traits!
Sandbox_ETW_AffinitySystem_tooltip:
Defines if the Affinity System is enabled for some traits tied to systems and some complex ones (for example, weight, Fear of Locations system, Herbalist, or Sleep System).
The Affinity system makes it easier to hold onto traits you picked during character creation, both negative and positive. With it enabled, you halve (modifiable) the speed at which you lose these traits, and double (also modifiable) the speed at which you earn these traits
Sandbox_ETW_AsthmaticCounter_tooltip: The value on the counter you should reach to lose the asthmatic trait. Running or exercising in cold temperatures decreases the counter; the colder it is, the faster the decrease. If you're outside, it decreases even faster. If you are a smoker, it decreases even faster. Additionally, being a smoker slowly decreases the counter when you run, even if the weather is fine. Reaching the counter removes the trait. The counter slowly increases by itself as long as you're not running or sprinting and breathing air warmer than 0 degrees Celsius. On top of that, it increases based on your Fitness level and current endurance level. Being a smoker halves the increase rate. Having the asthmatic trait halves it again

Sandbox_ETW_Bloodlust_tooltip: This allows you to gain a benefit by filling and maintaining a bloodlust meter. The bloodlust meter is soft-capped at 72 hours and can be filled by killing zombies. The closer the zombies are, the more quickly the meter will fill. When you're above half of the meter, every hour it will give you progress towards the bloodlust perk; when it's below, it'll remove progress. The bloodlust meter naturally decays by 1 every hour. Having bloodied clothes helps the process

Sandbox_ETW_BraverySystemKills_tooltip:
Here you set up how many kills you need to get to max out your bravery system. Melee kills count twice for progress. Progression is as follows: Cowardly -> Fear of Blood -> Pacifist -> Adrenaline Junkie -> Brave -> Desensitized
You need to have previous trait gone (if it's negative) or present (if it's positive) to earn/lose next trait In progression.
Amounts to reach each stage are as follows:
Cowardly: 10% of max kills
Fear of Blood: 20% of max kills
Pacifist: 30% of max kills
Adrenaline Junkie: 40% of max kills
Brave: 60% of max kills
Desensitized: 100% of max kills
Example: Max kills is set to 1000. You start with Cowardly. You need 100 kills to remove it. If you get 50 melee kills, it'll be removed. The same is true if you get 40 melee kills (x2 = 80 kills for the counter) and 20 firearms kills
Sandbox_ETW_BraverySystemRemovesOtherFea: Bravery System Removes Other Fear Perks
If enabled, getting desensitized through the Bravery system will also remove other fear perks like Pluviophile, Homichlophobia, Agoraphobic, and Claustrophobic, and prevent you from gaining them

Sandbox_ETW_CatEyesCounter_tooltip: This allows you to gain points by seeing and observing squares within a certain radius of your character. The number of points you earn is influenced by factors such as the time of day, the darkness of the square, and whether you and the square are inside or outside. The more squares you see and the darker they are, the more points you will earn. Having Eagle Eyed doubles the gain. Making a kill at night triggers extra execution of function responsible for gaining progress (so instead of getting progress 1 time / minute you can get progress 3 times per minute, for example)

Sandbox_ETW_DelayedTraitsSystemDefaultDe: Default delay (in hours) for traits to appear/disappear. For example, if set to 240, when you qualify for a new trait, you'll have a 1 in 240 chance to gain/lose it in the first hour. If it fails, the chance becomes 1 in 239 the next hour, and so on
Sandbox_ETW_DelayedTraitsSystemDefaultSt: Additional delay (in hours) stacked on top of the default delay for 'free' traits obtained at the start of the game. For example, starting with 9 Strength would usually grant Hoarder for free. If the Delayed Traits system is enabled, with a Default Delay of 240 and Additional Delay for Starting Traits of 480, you won't get Hoarder at the start. Instead, it goes into the table with a maximum delay of 720 hours. So, you'll have a 1 in 720 chance to get it in the first hour, and so on
Sandbox_ETW_DelayedTraitsSystem_tooltip:
This system allows you to gain/lose traits in a more random and less predictable way. When you qualify to add/remove a trait, it doesn't happen instantly. Instead, it's added to a table with a delay in hours (based on sandbox settings below). Every hour, the game rolls to determine if you gain/lose each trait in this table (each trait is rolled separately). You have a 1 in X chance to gain/lose the trait every hour. If the roll fails, X is reduced by 1. So the longer you go, the higher the chances that the trait you earned will manifest.
Technical note: Traits that rely on skill levels will be unlocked as described above. However, traits that rely on internal counters added by this mod (e.g., Prone To Illness, Weak Stomach, Outdoorsman, Cat Eyes, etc.) will unlock the next time their internal counters increase. This is because coding a separate unlock mechanism for these specific traits would be complex and unnecessary. For example, if you qualify for Cat Eyes and it's added to the Delayed Traits Table, you won't get it immediately. Instead, you'll get it as soon as the Cat Eyes counter increases next time (e.g., the closest evening/night).
Sandbox_ETW_EagleEyedDistance_tooltip: At what distance must a zombie be to count this as a kill to Eagle-Eyed kill counter. For vanilla would recommend leaving at 20, for mods that add good firearms (Gunfighter + Brita for example), would recommend setting to 25 or so
Sandbox_ETW_FearOfLocationsExclusiveFear: If enabled, you will only ever have Claustrophobic OR Agoraphobic, whichever has the lower counter
Sandbox_ETW_FearOfLocationsSystemCounter: Fear Of Locations Counter Decrease Multiplier

Controls how fast the counter decreases when you are unhappy (50%+) or stressed (50%+). Since you are more often normal than unhappy or stressed, it's recommended not to set this value too low. The formula for how much the counter decreases every minute is: 1 * (1 + unhappiness(0-1)) + (1 * stress(0-1)) * multiplier. At minimum, you lose 0 * multiplier; at maximum, you lose 4 * multiplier

Counter = amount of minutes you need to spend outside/inside to lose the respective trait, Agoraphobic or Claustrophobic. Being outside/inside when stressed or unhappy will decrease the counter. Reaching a negative counter value will GAIN you the appropriate trait. Reaching a positive counter value will get rid of the appropriate trait, being in between -counter and +counter will result in no change. The lower boundary is -2x of the counter, and the upper boundary is 2x of the set value here
Sandbox_ETW_FearOfLocationsSystemPassive: Fear of Locations Passive Counter Decay

If you have an issue managing both Agoraphobic and Claustrophobic traits simultaneously, you can set up passive decay using this option. This slowly decays the opposite counter based on whether you're outside/inside every minute, regardless of your mental state. For example, setting this to 0.1 and being inside will gradually reduce your fear of outside by adding 0.1 to the outside counter every minute. Setting it to 0 will have no effect on counters. Recommended values range from 0.1 to 0.5

Sandbox_ETW_SleepSystem_tooltip:
Enables obtaining/losing sleep-related traits, Wakeful and Sleepyhead.
---General description---
Mod tracks at which hours you like to sleep, and as long as you sleep within around those hours, you reinforce your healthy sleep schedule. If you sleep outside of it, you lose some schedule integrity. Not sleeping for more than 24 hours also starts to damage your sleep schedule. Mod tracks at which hours you like to sleep by checking the midpoint of your last sleep, so it's possible to shift your schedule to different hours.
---Technical description, don't read this if you don't want to meta-game much---
Every time you sleep, the mod tracks the midpoint of your sleep. For example, if you sleep between 23:00 and 05:30, the midpoint would be 03:45, and it would be your optimal sleeping hour. If you sleep within +-6 hours of this time, you gain progress to your SleepHealthiness bar, which ranges from -200 to 200. A check is made every 10 minutes, adding +0.167 to the bar if sleeping within the correct schedule, essentially giving +1 for every hour of correct sleep. Sleeping outside this schedule removes 0.167 from the bar every 10 minutes. After not sleeping for more than 24 hours, you start losing -0.167 every ten minutes. If your bar falls below -100, you get Sleepyhead. If it's above 100, you get Wakeful. Starting with either trait sets the starting value of the bar to its maximum or minimum point: +200 for Wakeful and -200 for Sleepyhead
Sandbox_ETW_SmokerCounter_tooltip:
Upon reaching this value on the counter, you'll get the Smoker trait. When dropping to the opposite of it, you'll lose it. Counter boundaries are -2x the counter to 2x the counter.

How it works: Every smoke you take increases your addiction counter. The longer breaks you take between smokes, the less the increase. Smoking while being panicked or stressed increases the counter much faster, based on the level of panic and stress. Not smoking slowly decays the counter. Being panicked or stressed slows the decay rate

Sandbox_WZDirector_MigrateCooldown_toolt:
Time required to pass before the Migrate Event can trigger.
The cooldown is constantly refreshed while the number of zombies is at, or above the %AAAAFFZombie Threshold%FFFFFF.
Value is in in-game minutes.
Sandbox_WZDirector_MigrateDistance_toolt:
This value determines how large of an area to give to the world sound.
Make sure to adjust the vanilla option Zombie Follow Distance to match.
Zombies inside a 120 radius of the world sound's location ignore the sound.
%DDDD00Setting this value too high can cause performance issues%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZDirector_MigrateEnabled_toolti:
When enabled (checked), allows the director to send out world sounds to attract distant zombies to a random location around the player.
%DDDD00This event is currently hardcoded to be disabled in MP%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZDirector_MigrateZombieThreshol: The director will only send out the world sound when there are less than this many active zombies.
Sandbox_WZDirector_PullEnabled_tooltip: When enabled (checked), allows the director to randomly pull zombies to a random location around the player, inside a radius, when the player has been unseen for a period of time.
Sandbox_WZDirector_PullMaxRadius_tooltip:
The starting and maximum size of the radius.
Upon being seen, the radius reverts to this value.
Sandbox_WZDirector_PullMinRadius_tooltip:
The smallest the radius can be.
Every in-game minute while you remain unseen, after the unseen time limit has been reached, the radius decreases by 1% of Max Radius.
Sandbox_WZDirector_PullUnseenTime_toolti:
Player must remain unseen for this period of time before the director can begin pulling zombies, and shrinking the radius.
Value is in in-game minutes.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_AllowCrawlers_tool:
When enabled (checked), crawlers are allowed to be in hordes.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler.
Without the Reflection Enabler:
- All zombies are considered Fast Shamblers.
- This option is forcefully disabled.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_AllowFastShamblers:
When enabled (checked), fast shamblers are allowed to be in hordes.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler.
Without the Reflection Enabler:
- All zombies are considered Fast Shamblers
- This option is forcefully enabled.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_AllowShamblers_too:
When enabled (checked), shamblers are allowed to be in hordes.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler.
Without the Reflection Enabler:
- All zombies are considered Fast Shamblers.
- This option is forcefully disabled.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_AllowSprinters_too:
When enabled (checked), sprinters are allowed to be in hordes.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler.
Without the Reflection Enabler:
- All zombies are considered Fast Shamblers.
This option is forcefully disabled.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_CreateJoinMergeDis:
The maximum distance at which zombies will create/join/merge hordes.

%FF0000Increase this value to increase the speed at which hordes form/grow%FFFFFF.
%00FF00Decrease this value to to decrease the speed at which hordes form/grow%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_GroupBySpeed_toolt:
When enabled (checked), zombies can only join hordes that match their speed.
Only reads the speedType variable, so mods that alter the animation speeds and do not correctly set the zombie's speedType to match will conflict.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler, and will be forcefully disabled without it.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_HordeLimit_tooltip:
The maximum number of hordes that are allowed to exist.
In multiplayer, this is per player.
%AAAAFFSet to 0 to disable.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_HordeSize_tooltip:
The largest size a horde can grow to.
When merging is enabled, this is ignored.
%AAAAFFSet this value to 0 to allow hordes to be of any size.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_HordesMerge_toolti: When enabled (checked), hordes can join together to become a single, bigger horde.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_Hordes_tooltip: When enabled (checked), Wandering Zombie's horde features will turn on.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_LeaveDistance_tool:
Zombies that are at least (Leave Distance + Create/Join/Merge Distance) away from the horde will leave the horde.
%FF0000Set this to 0 to prevent zombies from leaving hordes%FFFFFF.
%DDDD00Increase this value to increase the average size of hordes%FFFFFF.
%00FF00Decrease this value to decrease the average size of hordes%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_MergeCooldown_tool:
The amount of time that must pass before a horde is allowed to merge.
This value is multiplied by the number of followers in a horde.

%00FF00Increase this value to reduce the speed at which hordes grow in size%FFFFFF.
%FF0000Decrease this value to increase the speed at which hordes grow in size%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_MoveCooldownHordeS:
This value is multiplied by the size of the horde before being added to the result of the above settings.

%00FF00Increase this value to reduce difficulty%FFFFFF.
%FF0000Decrease this value to increase difficulty%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WZHordeZombie_WorldAgeHours_tool: Hordes will not start to form until the world is at least this old.
Sandbox_WZPerformance_SandboxVarsUpdateF:
Controls the frequency (milliseconds) of Wandering Zombies updating it's Sandbox Options.
Time periods and destruction are also calculated during this update.
You should not need to change this value.
Sandbox_WZPerformance_ZombieProcessLimit:
The number of zombies that Wandering Zombies performs an update on each frame.
This does not limit the amount of zombies Wandering Zombies has control over, as the update continues where it stopped on the last frame.
You should not need to change this value.
Sandbox_WZShared_ChebyshevDistance_toolt:
When enabled (checked), Wandering Zombies will use Chebyshev for distance instead of Euclidean.
Chebyshev measures distance in a square.
Euclidean measures distance in a circle.
Chebyshev distance may slightly improve performance.
Sandbox_WZShared_DumbZombiesExplore_tool:
When enabled (checked), all zombies are allowed to explore.
When disabled (unchecked), only smart zombies are allowed to explore.

%DDDD00This option requires the mod Reflection Enabler.
Without the Reflection Enabler:
- All zombies are considered dumb.
- This option is forcefully enabled.%FFFFFF
Sandbox_WZShared_ExploreDestructive_tool: When enabled (checked), exploring zombies will destroy objects in their path.
Sandbox_WZShared_ForcePathfind_tooltip:
%AAAAFFNever%FFFFFF: Let the game decide when pathfinding should be used.
%AAAAFFIndoors%FFFFFF: Attempt to force pathfinding for indoor zombies.
%AAAAFFAlways%FFFFFF: Attempt to force pathfinding for all zombies.
Sandbox_WZShared_ForcedExploreChance_too:
Chance that a zombie passing through a building will stop, and explore it.
Zombies that come to a stop inside a building will always explore, as long as exploring is enabled.
Sandbox_WZShared_HoursSurvived_tooltip: The minimum amount of hours a player needs to of survived before zombies will be able to use the player as a target of homing.
Sandbox_WZShared_MoveCooldownInitial_too:
When enabled (checked), the move cooldown is applied to a zombie the moment Wandering Zombies becomes aware of it.
This will %DDDD00prevent zombies immediately moving%FFFFFF the moment they load in. (From starting/loading a game, moving around the world, being teleported (Admin / RV Interiors)).
Sandbox_WZShared_OutOfCellPaths_tooltip: When enabled (checked), zombies are allowed to select a path that leads to them walking out of the loaded area / active cell.
Sandbox_WZShared_OutOfCellThreshold_tool: Only allow Out Of Cell Paths when the number of zombies exceeds this value.
Sandbox_WZShared_RepeatExplore_tooltip: When enabled (checked), a zombie that has finished exploring will start exploring again if they are not on the ground floor.
Sandbox_WZShared_RoomExploreLimit_toolti:
Maximum random number of times a zombie will select a room from the building they're in to explore.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_WZShared_TryStopVirtual_tooltip:
When enabled (checked), zombie movement will be monitored to try and prevent them from walking out of the loaded area.
This does not apply to sprinters due to the possibility of sprinters keeping up with the player, resulting in an increase over time of the sprinters in the area.
Sandbox_WZShared_WanderForwards_tooltip:
When enabled (checked), the random location chosen for wandering will be locked to a position +/- 45 degrees in the direction the zombie is facing.
If enabled, recommend either turning off %AAAAFFOut Of Cell Paths%FFFFFF, or increasing %AAAAFFOut Of Cell Threshold%FFFFFF.
Since this still chooses a random location and passes it to the game's finding, %DDDD00zombies won't necessarily move forwards%FFFFFF due to fences, buildings, etc.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_AllowCrawlers_t: When enabled, crawlers are allowed to be in hordes
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_AllowFastShambl: When enabled, fast shamblers are allowed to be in hordes
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_AllowShamblers_: When enabled, slow shamblers are allowed to be in hordes
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_AllowSprinters_: When enabled, sprinters are allowed to be in hordes
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_ChanceDropdown_:
%AAAAFFStatic%FFFFFF: The value chosen below is always used.
%AAAAFFRandom%FFFFFF: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is used. The value is randomised when the period of activity is calculated.

If Min is greater than Max, Max will be used as the minimum.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_ChanceMax_toolt: This is only used if %AAAAFFChance: Mode%FFFFFF is set to %AAAAFFRandom%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_CooldownHoursDr:
%AAAAFFStatic%FFFFFF: The value chosen below is always used.
%AAAAFFRandom%FFFFFF: A random value from Min to Max (inclusive) is used. The value is randomised when the period of activity is calculated.

Min is allowed to be greater than Max, so ranges over midnight can be used.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_CooldownHoursMa: This is only used when %AAAAFFCooldown Hours: Mode%FFFFFF is set to %AAAAFFRandom%FFFFFF.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_CooldownHoursMi:
The amount of time that must elapse before the next period of activity.
If this value is not set to a multiple of 24, or is randomised to a value that is not a multiple of 24, the remainder is used to adjust Start Hour for that period of activity.
For example, if Start Hour is set to 0 (12:00am), and Cooldown Hours is set to 26, the next Start Hour would be 2am.
Sandbox_WanderingZombies_Destructive_too:
%AAAAFFAlways%FFFFFF: Zombies will always attack objects in their path.
%AAAAFFIndoors%FFFFFF: Zombies considered indoors will attack objects in their path.
%AAAAFFNever%FFFFFF: Zombies will not attack objects in their path.
%AAAAFFRandom%FFFFFF: Randomly select one of the above, when the period of activity is calculated.

The vanilla destruction settings do NOT have an effect on this setting.
Setting this value to %FF0000anything other than %AAAAFFNever %FF0000increases difficulty%FFFFFF.

Recommended setting is %AAAAFFAlways%FFFFFF:
- It increases the ambiance.
- It makes undamaged houses valuable.
- It opens more paths for zombies to use.

Chance is only rolled when the timer has elapsed and the horde is ready to move
Max Travel applies to fleeing hordes

Sandbox_WanderingZombies_DropdownFleeSta:
At what hour should lone zombies flee from the nearest player
If set to static, uses Flee Start Hour: Max
If set to random, Flee Start Hour is randomised after the time period has elapsed using the below values (inclusive)
Supports Min/Max order switching, for example (6pm -> 6am): Min = 18, Max = 6
Multiple periods of activity can occur in a single day
Periods of activity can chain, for example:
Start Hour Min: 18, Start Hour Max: 6 (6pm -> 6am)
Total Hours Min: 0, Total Hours Max: 12
The above can lead to a 24 hour period of activity if Start Hour is randomised to 6am, and Total Hours is randomised to 12

Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankAimSkillR: Point Blank - Aim skill reduction % multiplier
"(NOT YET IMPLEMENTED) Cooldown Reduction = Cooldown duration * AimSkillReductionMultiplier * (AimingSkill/10)"
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankBonusDama: Point Blank Bonus Damage Multiplier (ONLY USED WHEN InstantKill is DISABLED)

This multiplier is applied to your bonus damage from above. This does NOT affect BASE damage value, ONLY bonus damage. See equation below: 

 TotalDamage = BaseDamage + PointBlankDamage
 PointBlankDamage = (Max(BaseDamage,PointBlankMinimumBonusDamage) * PointBlankBonusDamageMultiplier )
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankCooldownD: Point Blank - How long until point blank can trigger again. Reduced by aim skill
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankCooldownT: "(NOT YET IMPLEMENTED) When cooldown is active, this value determines chance for point blank to hit again. Rises to 100% as cooldown refresh approaches"
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankDisableMu: Point Blank - Disable Multiplayer Command Updates

For debugging purposes. You shouldn't change this. But if you're having server/client/networking issues, this will disable synchronous server/client updates. Without this, when you pointblank kill a zed, there can be a delay for them appear dead for other players.
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankEffective: Zombies shot upon below this range will be affected by point blank damage

Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankMinTicksB: Point Blank - Min Ticks Between Point Blank Kills

Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankMinimumBo: Point Blank Minimum Bonus Damage (ONLY USED WHEN InstantKill is DISABLED)

This is the minimum amount bonus damage that is applied. 
IE, if your damage is .0001, it would increase the bonus damage to .2 
 See equation below: 

 TotalDamage = BaseDamage + PointBlankDamage
 PointBlankDamage = (Max(BaseDamage,PointBlankMinimumBonusDamage) * PointBlankBonusDamageMultiplier )
Sandbox_pointblankhf_PointBlankUseExperi: If true, hit detection is WAY more lenient. It won't matter if you are moving, or how long you have been aiming, they will just die, if within range (or point blank damage will take effect).

Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BloodinessDamageL: The limit for the damage boost when bloody.\n\nSet as multiplier, e.g. 0.5 means 50% more damage at max.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BloodinessDamageM:
How much your bloodiness impacts your damage.

The damage is added via formula:
weapon damage * (bloodiness * BloodinessDamageMultiplier))
Bloodiness is calculated by summing up body, clothing and weapon bloodiness.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BloodinessImpactO:
Bloodiness impact factor on bad moodle reduces when killing a zombie.

The multiplier formula:
1 + (bloodiness * BloodinessImpactOnReduces)

Set 0 to always reduce exactly the set values
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BodyBloodinessFac:
How impactful body bloodiness is.

It's calculated by summing up bloodiness from all body parts, then dividing it by the total count of body parts.

Set 0 to not consider body bloodiness
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BoredomGain_toolt: How much boredom to add every 10 ingame minutes in the state of bloodlust.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_BoredomReduce_too: Minimum boredom to reduce with every kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_CigarStressReduce: Minimum cigarette stress to reduce with every kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_ClothingBloodines:
How impactful clothing bloodiness is.

It's calculated by summing up relative bloodiness from all worn items, then dividing it by the total count of body parts.
(The relative bloodiness is calculated by multiplying clothing bloodiness by the count of body parts it covers.)

Set 0 to not consider clothing bloodiness
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_DisablePanic_tool: Disable panic in the state of bloodlust.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_EarnBloodinessThr:
How bloody your character must be for a kill to be considered bloody.

Character bloodiness is calculated by summing up body, clothing and weapon bloodiness.
It can be higher than 1.

Set 0 to consider every single kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_EarnDecreaseBlood:
Whatever to decrease bloody kills every 10 ingame minutes if your character is not bloody enough.

Note that this also happens when sleeping.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_EarnIt_tooltip: Enable the ability to earn the trait.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_EarnKiilsThreshol:
How many bloody* kills your character must do to earn the trait.

* A kill is considered bloody if your overall bloodiness is higher than the set threshold.
Note that a kill must also be performed in melee combat.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_MassiveDamageOnBl: Make your first hit after a long break deal a lot of damage (Basically an instant kill)
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_MaxMinutesNoKill_:
Maximum ingame minutes your character can be fine without killing anyone.

The time is decreased by multiplying it with 'cleanliness' (1 - bloodiness)
Bloodiness is calculated by summing up body, clothing and weapon bloodiness.
It can be higher than 1, in which case MinHoursNoKill is used.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_MinMinutesNoKill_: Minimum ingame minutes your character will be fine after a kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_StressGain_toolti: How much stress to add every 10 ingame minutes in the state of bloodlust.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_StressReduce_tool: Minimum stress to reduce with every kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_UnhappinessGain_t: How much unhappiness to add every 10 ingame minutes in the state of bloodlust.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_UnhappinessReduce: Minimum unhappiness to reduce with every kill.
Sandbox_BloodlustTrait_WeaponBloodinessF:
How impactful held weapon bloodiness is.

It just gets the primary hand weapon bloodiness. This means if the weapon is 100% bloody, it's valued the same as if every single part of your body was 100% bloody, so you might want to set this modifier lower.

Set 0 to not consider weapon bloodiness
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_CooldownRandomness:
Applies randomness to the cooldown time.
For example, 0.5 randomness means the cooldown can be 50% longer or shorter.

Note that this setting, unlike others, is updated after a change only when a new character is created or the ability is used.

Set 0 for no randomness
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_Cooldown_tooltip:
How many ingame minutes must pass before the ability could be used again.

One day is 1440 minutes.
One week is 10080 minutes.

Set 0 for no cooldown
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_DamageChance_toolt:
The chance to damage a zombie when pushing it.

For example, 0.15 means there is a 15% chance for a zombie to be damaged.
Set 1 to always deal damage
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_DamageMax_tooltip: Maximum damage to deal to a zombie.\n\nMaximum health of a zombie is 2.0
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_DamageMin_tooltip: Minimum damage to deal to a zombie.\n\nMaximum health of a zombie is 2.0
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_EarnIt_tooltip: Add the trait when a specified strength level is achieved.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_EnduranceCost_tool:
How much endurance to reduce when the ability is used.

<75 is Moderate Exertion
<50 is High Exertion
<25 is Excessive Exertion
<10 is Exhausted
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_EnduranceMin_toolt:
The minimum endurance required to use the ability.

<75 is Moderate Exertion
<50 is High Exertion
<25 is Excessive Exertion
<10 is Exhausted
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_FatigueAddUp_toolt:
How much fatigue (need to sleep) to add when the ability is used.

>60 is Drowsy
>70 is Tired
>80 is Very Tired
>90 is Ridiculously Tired
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_FatigueMax_tooltip:
The maximum level of tiredness up to which the ability could be used.

>60 is Drowsy
>70 is Tired
>80 is Very Tired
>90 is Ridiculously Tired
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_HitActivationDista:
Maximum distance to count zombies on for hit activation.

Note that this is separate from Drag Down activation, which happens when zombies surround and eat you alive.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_HitActivationZombi:
How many zombies must be nearby to activate the ability when hit.

Note that this is separate from Drag Down activation, which happens when zombies surround and eat you alive.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_HitActivation_tool:
Activate the ability when hit if the criteria are met.

Note that this is separate from Drag Down activation, which happens when zombies surround and eat you alive.
You don't really have to enable this if Drag Down is enabled (Vanilla Zombie Lore tab)
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_PushDistance_toolt:
How close a zombie must be to get affected.

Note that the character will still be staggered from a hit, meaning other zombies might get them again, neglecting the last push.
With the default setting of 2.5 you have just the time to start moving and might still be caught again.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_SoundRadius_toolti: The radius of a sound which is emitted when the ability is used.\n\nSet 0 to disable
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_StrengthRequiremen: The level of strength required to earn the perk if it wasn't picked during character creation.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_UseChanceReroll_to: If the chance check failed, the next attempt will be only after this amount of real seconds.
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_UseChance_tooltip:
The chance to use the ability, avoiding death.

For example, 0.15 means there is a 15% chance to use the ability.

Set 1 to always use
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_UsesLimit_tooltip: How many times can the character use this ability.\n\nSet 0 for no limit
Sandbox_LastPushTrait_ZombiesLimit_toolt: How many zombies will be affected.\n\nSet 0 for no limit

Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BaseEatTime_tool:
This value is used to calculate how long a body takes to be eaten.
It is in real world seconds.
The actual time taken to consume a corpse is adjusted by:
- Size of the body relative(ish) to a human.
- Number of zombies eating the body.
- Current game speed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyAgeMultiplie: Bodies will have their age (world hours) multiplied by this value, which is then added to the smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyDispersionAn:
This angle is used to determine whether a zombie falls inside an area that is projected from bodies in the direction of the wind, up to the smell distance.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyIndoorCheck_: When enabled (checked), only zombies in the same building as a body are capable of smelling it.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyMaxDistance_: Maximum potential distance of dead body smell
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodySizeImpactsS: When enabled (checked), the size of the body has an effect on the distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyStartDistanc: Body smell distance will always start at this value.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyTemperatureP:
This value is divided by the current temperature, to get a multiplier that adjusts the result of [Start Distance + Age Multiplier].
This value is in celsius.
Set to 0 to disable temperature having an effect.
At default, temperatures above 26C increase the distance bodies can be smelled by zombies, while temperatures below 26C decrease the distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_BodyWindSpeedMul:
This value is used to determine how much impact the wind speed has on the smell of bodies.
Higher values increase the effect.
Wind has a significant impact on smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_CanSmellPlayer_t: When enabled (checked), zombies will be able to smell players.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_EatCooldownMulti:
This value controls how often a zombie can eat.
At 1.0, a zombie will not eat again for the same amount of game time they spent eating.
The cooldown increases as they eat, and does not require a body to be fully consumed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_EatSyncFrequency:
Time in milliseconds between syncing eat progress.
Values greater than 1000 may reduce the accuracy of Base Eat Time.
This is intended for multiplayer usage, to reduce network traffic and log spam caused by RPC.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_FogMultiplier_to:
Adjusts how much fog increases smell distance.
Higher values increase the effect.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_ItemDestroyChanc: When a body is consumed, every individual item has this chance of being destroyed.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerBloodMulti: The amount of blood on a player, and on items in their inventory, will be multiplied by this value, which is then added to smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerDispersion:
This angle is used to determine whether a zombie falls inside an area that is projected from players in the direction of the wind, up to the smell distance.
Set to 0 disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerInterruptF: When enabled (checked), zombies will stop feeding and target the player, if they smell the player.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerMaxDistanc: Maximum potential distance of player's smell.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerStartDista: Player smell distance will always start at this value.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_PlayerWindSpeedM:
This value is used to determine how much impact the wind speed has on the smell of the player.
Higher values increase the effect.
Wind has a significant effect on smell distance.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_RainMultiplier_t:
Adjusts how much rain reduces smell distance.
Higher values increase the effect.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_RandomSensitivit: When enabled (checked), zombies are assigned a random sensitivity to smell.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_TemperaturePeak_:
Temperature above this value increases smell distance.
Temperature below this value decreases smell distance.
This value is in celsius.
Set to 0 to disable.
Sandbox_StarvingZombies_ZMultiplier_tool:
Z coordinate of zombies, bodies and players are multiplied by this value.
When this value is greater than 1.0, it artificially increases the distance between zombies and bodies/players that are on different levels.
Sandbox_allowPortableJukeboxKeys_tooltip: If this is enabled, then you will be able to access the data of saved jukebox locations by using the inventory context menu of your key ring. Interact with any jukebox to store the key to its data for remote access.
Sandbox_disablePowerRequirement_tooltip: Disable the requirement for jukeboxes to have a supply of electricity; the power of music will be sufficient to keep a jukebox alive.
Sandbox_enableJukeboxNutrition_tooltip: Jukebox music can be food for both the soul AND the body! If you enable this feature, players will gain nutrition when they hear a track begin in a jukebox. The amount of nutrition gained per track is determined by the settings on this page. This setting applies the same exploit prevention strategies that are used for Jukebox Therapy.
Sandbox_enableJukeboxTherapy_tooltip: Give your music a degree in psychology! If you enable this feature, players will recover in a variety of ways whenever a True Music track begins in an audible jukebox. This feature is designed to prevent exploitation; players cannot benefit repeatedly by rapidly skipping tracks or playing 20 jukeboxes at a time. Reduction values below are normalized on a scale from 0 to 100 percent reduction (relative to the maximum value a state can take).
Sandbox_enableLifestyleFavoriteEffects_t: If Lifestyle is installed on your server and this feature is enabled, players who are dancing to the music of at least one audible jukebox will benefit from Lifestyle moodle effects as though they are hearing their favorite music played by an expert. This effect only occurs while they dance in order to circumvent a possible conflict between the availability of Lifestyle's normal Dance option and the availability of our version.
Sandbox_enableLifestyleIntegrations_tool: If Lifestyle is installed on your server and this feature is enabled, Lifestyle tracks will mute True Music Jukebox tracks, and our tracks will mute their tracks. You will also be able to trigger random styles of Lifestyle dancing whenever Lifestyle's built-in dance option is unavailable in the context menu.
Sandbox_enableStaticPlayerHealth_tooltip: Enable this setting in order to ensure that player weights will not change from day to day, regardless of nutrition. Additionally, players will recover healthy levels of calories, carbohydrates, proteins, and lipids every day. The purpose of this setting is to promote endless partying without fear of death by starvation; it does not stop zombies from eating people.
Sandbox_forceThreeDimensionalAudio_toolt: Forces all players on the server to use Project Zomboid's 3D sound mode, which causes sound to be impacted by rooms and walls. We think this makes the music sound worse in a lot of cases, so we recommend leaving this off and allowing your players to choose their own sound mode on an individual basis using their in-game Mod Options. By default, this mod uses its own custom 3D sound mode.
Sandbox_heroStarterTracks_tooltip: How many random cassettes and vinyls should a jukebox hero gain at character creation? <RGB:1.0,0.6,0.0>
Sandbox_ignoreDistanceWhenPlaying_toolti: If this option is enabled, songs will begin no matter how far players are from their source in order to maximize sync between all clients at all times. However, due to how Zomboid handles the creation of sound, clients may briefly stutter when songs start. If you disable this option, clients will not be in sync until they are within range of a jukebox while it is changing tracks, but they will not play tracks that are not audible to them, reducing the frequency of this stutter.

Sandbox_maximumJukeboxesDeliveredOnConne: This setting limits the number of jukeboxes for which newly connected players will automatically receive data in order to reduce the likelihood of server strain from too many players trying to sync too many active jukeboxes. <LINE>  <RGB:1.0,0.3,0.3> Be aware that there is a limit to how many jukeboxes any server can easily sync per player.

Sandbox_TLOU_BloaterSpawn_tooltip:
Bloaters are seen as legends by many due to their rarity among infected types. If a Clicker manages to survive over the years, sustaining its body and the Cordycep within, it evolves into a colossus with thick skin protected by Cordyceps patches.
No one wants to contemplate what would happen to a person if they were caught by this creature, so approaching it is out of the question.

Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerBurnRate_tooltip: Dictates how fast a Clicker will burn and die from fire.

Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerHP_tooltip: 0 means default vanilla zombie health (depends on Clicker toughness).
Sandbox_TLOU_ClickerSpawn_tooltip:
Clickers evolve from Stalkers into an even more dangerous state. Their inhuman strength makes them extremely perilous to approach; anyone too close could find themselves dead in mere seconds.
The cries of struggle have long been replaced with a clicking noise, used to replace their lost eyes due to the Cordyceps eating through them.
Fortunately, this alteration makes them slower than simple Runners and Stalkers. However, they will move in unpredictable ways their arms, catching you whenever they get close enough to you.

A value of 0 deactivates the extra damage, a value of 1 means 100% extra damage, a value of 2 means 200% extra damage...

Sandbox_TLOU_GrabbyClickers_tooltip: Clickers can grab you, making you unable to move. You can save yourself with short blades if you time it well. By default is deactivated due to how unfair it can be but if you want an even harder challenge, go for it.
Sandbox_TLOU_HideIndoorsUpdates_tooltip: Defines how often Infected will check buildings to move towards or roam outside at night. This number shouldn't be kept too low but if you set it too high the Infected might not have time to go in buildings or roam outside at night. On the other hand, you can set it to higher values so they have time to roam around the map. (such as map sounds like alarms or gun shots)
Sandbox_TLOU_HideIndoors_tooltip: All the infected besides Runners have a tendency to hide from the sun within the dark corners of buildings. This makes exploration of a building particularly dangerous while the streets are safer. Make sure to pay attention to your surrondings when exploring.
Sandbox_TLOU_MaxDistanceToCheck_tooltip: Defines the max distance an Infected will check for buildings. The higher the value, the harder the performance impact might be (unsure how hard it hits performances).
Sandbox_TLOU_NoPushBloaters_tooltip: Makes players unable to push Bloaters.
Sandbox_TLOU_NoPushClickers_tooltip: Makes players unable to push Clickers.
Sandbox_TLOU_NoStompClickers_tooltip: Makes players unable to head stomp Clickers with their foot. This means Clickers won't take any damage from stomping with your feet.
Sandbox_TLOU_OneShotClickers_tooltip: Clickers will one shot you, this trait is definitely the most punishing one.
Sandbox_TLOU_OnlyUnexplored_tooltip: Infected will go hide only in unexplored areas. If unchecked then expect some guests in your house. If you've explored every buildings in an area, this could also mean you would find all the Infected types in the street which isn't ideal, especially with respawn on.

Runners are dangerous and fast humans recently infected by the Cordyceps fungus. They can quickly overwhelm you with their sheer speed and numbers.
You may hear them talking and struggling from within, with the soul of the host likely still present but unable to control their body.

Sandbox_TLOU_Separation_TankyInfected_to:
[THIS OPTION DOES NOT DO ANYTHING]
Clickers and Bloaters use an armor system and react accordingly to the energy of the caliber of the gun used. Heavy melee weapons will break this armor easier but normal melee weapons are incapable of breaking through. When the armor breaks, the infected takes extra damage.
Each calibers have a minimum energy and a maxium energy. A caliber needs to have a higher minimum energy value than the required energy to break an infected armor. If only the maximum value is above the needed energy, a coin flip determines if the shot will damage the armor. Based on how high the energy of the caliber is, it will break through the armor better.

Sandbox_TLOU_StalkerSpawn_tooltip:
Stalkers evolve from Runners with the Cordycep fully taking over the host's body. They are quicker and stronger than simple Runners, often ambushing you by hiding inside buildings.
The human inside likely lost the battle against the fungi, and its cries of struggle are slowly being replaced by a distinctive clicking noise.

Deactivate by setting to 0, the value is in seconds and defines how long you can stand on the infected.

Players and infected will be staggered if they are standing on Clickers. Clickers can stagger Runners, Stalkers and Clickers.
Deactivate by setting to 0, the value is in seconds and defines how long you can stand on the infected.
Sandbox_TLOU_StandOnInfected_Runner_tool:

Sandbox_RedDays_phase_start_delay_enable: This is mainly for newly spawned players so players don't always start on the menstrual phase.
Sandbox_RedDays_phase_start_delay_lowerB: The shortest amount of days before your first period occurs.
Sandbox_RedDays_phase_start_delay_upperB: The maximum amount of days before your first period occurs.
Sandbox_RedDays_red_phase_duration_lower: The shortest possible duration (in days) for the red (menstruation) phase.
Sandbox_RedDays_red_phase_duration_upper: The longest possible duration (in days) for the red (menstruation) phase.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_abx_dose_cooldown_ho: How many hours a single antibiotic dose keeps working before the next dose is needed. Each dose's treatment effect drains steadily over this period.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_abx_pills_to_cure: ABX Pills Needed To Cure Stage 4
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_abx_pills_to_cure_to: How many antibiotic doses are required to fully clear Stage 4 toxic shock. Default 10 is about a 5-day course at 2 doses/day.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_abx_sleep_health_cap: With active antibiotics, Stage 4 cannot drop health below this percentage. Sleeping with antibiotics restores health up to this cap and will not kill you. Without antibiotics this cap does not apply.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_abx_suppress_window_: Hours after taking an antibiotic dose that full Stage 4 sickness drain is suppressed. Default is 12h to match 2-dose/day treatment cadence.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_complication_chance_: When pre-TSS infection is active, this is the hourly chance for a sudden complication. Higher values mean symptoms can worsen more often, especially when you are sick, tired, thirsty, or cold/overheated.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_enabled_tooltip: Enable or disable Red Days TSS progression and treatment mechanics.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_fever_nudge_strength: Percentage multiplier for how hard TSS pushes the fever above the vanilla Stage 4 sickness plateau (~38C). 0 disables the extra heat push entirely; 100 is standard nudge intensity. Body temperature is still primarily driven by the sickness moodle.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_lethal_enabled_toolt: If enabled, untreated Stage 3 can transition into Stage 4 toxic shock.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_min_stage3_hours: TSS: Min Time in Stage 3 Before Toxic Shock (Hours)
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_min_stage3_hours_too: Minimum in-game hours that must be spent in Stage 3 severe infection before Toxic Shock Syndrome (Stage 4) becomes eligible. TSS cannot occur before this threshold.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_recovery_hours_per_s: In-game hours of healing needed (tampon/pad removed, no antibiotics) to drop one TSS stage, e.g. Stage 3 to Stage 0 takes 3x this. Antibiotics double the speed while a dose is still active.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_risk_multiplier_pct_: Scales Stage 3 to Stage 4 risk gain. Lower is safer, higher is riskier.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage0_duration_lowe: Minimum in-game hours before tampon exposure can begin progressing into Stage 1 infection. Lower values make infection start sooner under continuous use.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage0_duration_uppe: Maximum time the uninfected state (Stage 0) can persist before progression to Stage 1 is forced. Higher values delay initial infection onset.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage1_duration_lowe: Minimum in-game hours before early infection (Stage 1) can progress into established infection (Stage 2). Lower values accelerate worsening.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage1_duration_uppe: Maximum time Stage 1 infection can persist before it is forced to progress into Stage 2. Higher values allow longer mild infection periods.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage2_duration_lowe: Minimum in-game hours before established infection (Stage 2) can progress into severe systemic illness (Stage 3). Lower values increase danger speed.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage2_duration_uppe: Maximum time Stage 2 infection can persist before progressing into Stage 3. Higher values slow severe illness onset.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage4_hp_drain_pct: TSS Stage 4 HP Drain While Awake (%)
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage4_hp_drain_pct_: Percentage multiplier for base HP drain during Stage 4 Toxic Shock Syndrome while awake. 100 = normal (0.15 HP/min base). 200 = double drain. 50 = half drain. Drain scales further with body temperature.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_stage4_sleep_hp_drai: TSS Stage 4 HP Drain While Asleep (%)

Percentage multiplier for base Stage 4 HP drain while the player is asleep, separate from the awake drain. 0 = no HP loss during sleep. Without antibiotics you can still die in your sleep; drain scales with body temperature like the awake value.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_tampon_grace_hours_t: How long a tampon can be worn before it starts contributing to TSS exposure.
Sandbox_RedDays_tss_warning_interval_min: How often TSS warning messages are shown while symptoms are active.

Sandbox_RealisticCold_BreachWeightCurtai: How much cold leaks through a curtained-but-otherwise-open opening. 0.3 is the default - curtains help but aren't perfect.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_BreachWeightDoor_t: How much cold leaks through a closed door. 1.2 is the default. Higher = drafty doors.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_BreachWeightGap_to: How much cold pours through large structural gaps (broken walls, holes). 1.4 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_BreachWeightWindow: How much cold leaks through a closed window. 0.8 is the default. Higher = windowed rooms get colder.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_CatchColdRateMulti: How quickly the catch-a-cold meter fills once you're past the threshold. 1.75 is the default. Higher = colds catch faster.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_CatchColdThreshold: Cold stage you need to reach before you can catch a cold. 1 = Chilly (easiest, most forgiving), 2 = Cold (default), 3 = Freezing, 4 = Hypothermia (only catch a cold if literally freezing to death).
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ChillyAirThreshold: Air temperature at which the chilly warning can start firing. Below this, the moodle considers you exposed. Default 16°C.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ChillyCoolingMulti: When clothing's cooling factor exceeds this fraction, you start to feel chilly. Lower = warning fires earlier (less protection feels colder sooner). 0.9 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ChillyInsulationTh: Average clothing insulation below which the chilly warning is allowed to fire. 1.5 is the default. Set higher to make the warning fire even with moderate clothing.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ClothingInsulation: How much warmth your clothes provide. 4 is the mod's baseline; lower means clothing protects less, higher means more. Below 1, even heavy gear feels thin; above 6, light layers feel like a winter coat.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ColdMedicineDecayP: How quickly the effect of cold medicine fades. 36 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ColdRecoverPerHour: How quickly a cold improves while resting and warm. 24 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ColdSicknessMultip: Scales how badly a cold affects you (sickness moodle, infection rate). 1.0 is baseline. Higher = colds feel like the flu.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ColdWorsenPerHour_: How quickly an untreated cold gets worse, in cold-strength points per game-hour. 45 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ConvectiveBridgeSt: Smoothes the warming-rate cliff right at normal body temperature. 1.0 is baseline. 0 disables the bridge, warming up from cold to normal feels fast, but heating past normal in hot air feels much slower.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_EnableFoodFreezing: Lets food freeze inside containers when the surrounding temperature drops below freezing. Experimental - may interact unpredictably with other food mods.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_EvapCoolingStrengt: How much sweat actually cools your body as it evaporates. 1.0 is baseline. 0 disables evaporative cooling entirely (sweat still soaks clothing but provides no cooling). Wind and dry air boost the effect; rain cancels most of it.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_ExposureCap_toolti: Maximum combined cold leakage allowed across all openings (windows + doors + gaps + curtains) in one room. Higher = drafty rooms can equalize to outdoor faster. 6.0 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_HeatDistanceExpone: How sharply heater warmth fades with distance. 1.0 is the default (linear). Higher = warmth stays close to the heater. Lower = heat reaches further.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_HeatTargetMaximum_: Warmest temperature any single heater will aim for in its room. 26°C is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_HypothermiaDamageI: Minimum game-hours between hypothermia damage ticks. Smaller = more frequent damage. 0.2 is the default (one tick every ~12 game-minutes).
Sandbox_RealisticCold_HypothermiaDamageP: Health lost per hypothermia damage tick. 0.2 is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_IndustrialHeaterSp: Percent chance an industrial heater appears in large industrial buildings. Set to 0 to disable industrial-heater spawns entirely.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_InsulationSpreadBi: Controls how strongly uneven loadouts (e.g. parka + bare legs) deviate from the simple body-wide average. 0.0 = pure average (all parts treated equally); 1.0 = always pulled toward the weakest part in cold and the most-trapping part in heat. 0.30 is the recommended middle ground.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_SealedPassiveTrans: Sealed Building - Passive Heat Transfer (1.0 = baseline)

How fast a fully sealed building (no broken windows, no open doors, no gaps) drifts toward the outside temperature through walls and ceiling. 1.0 is the mod's baseline. 0 = a sealed house holds its temperature forever; 2.0 = walls leak twice as fast even when sealed; 5.0 = even sealed homes equalize quickly. Has no effect on buildings with active leaks.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_SweatRateMultiplie: Scales how fast you produce sweat when overheating. 1.0 is the mod's baseline. Lower numbers mean less wetness from heat stress (and clothing stays drier); higher numbers mean you drench yourself faster.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_VehicleHeaterMaxDe: Vehicle Heater - Max Heat Above Outdoors (°C)
Maximum degrees above outdoor temperature that a running vehicle heater can produce. 25°C is the default.
Sandbox_RealisticCold_WarmingRateCapCPM_: Hard ceiling on how fast body temperature can rise from environmental warming (warm air, heaters, hot drinks combined). 0.5 °C/min is the default. Lower for slower recovery from cold; raise for instant warm-up at fires.
Sandbox_ImmersiveBlackouts_ElectricityCo: Cooldown (in hours) between possible electricity shutoffs or restorations.

Sandbox_ImmersiveBlackouts_IgnoreStartDa: If enabled, the mod will operate even when the water and electricity shutoff sandbox options are disabled.\nWill ignore the 'Days Before Shutdown' option.

Sandbox_ImmersiveBlackouts_ModReset_tool: Enabling this option will reset the mod's saved data.\nONLY ENABLE THIS IF YOU HAVE CHANGED THE DAY WHEN THE SHUTDOWNS WILL OCCUR IN SANDBOX OPTIONS > WORLD.\nIT WILL AUTOMATICALLY DISABLE AFTERWARDS.

Sandbox_SWSprintersOverTime_Delay_toolti: Delay the appearance of the first sprinters. In days.

Sandbox_SWSprintersOverTime_Reverse_tool: Decrease the Sprinter Percentage instead of increasing it. (100% at day one instead of 1%)
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertAtScreamPosition_: Enabled: zombies walk toward where the scream actually happened (the sprinter's position) — tactically coherent with what you hear. Disabled: v1.0 legacy behavior, the horde converges on YOUR position.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertNearbyZombies_too: If enabled, the scream uses the game’s sound system to alert zombies within a set radius. If disabled, the scream is only aesthetic — it scares the player but doesn’t affect horde AI. Great for immersive sound without changing difficulty.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_AlertRadius_tooltip: The size of the area, in tiles, where zombies will hear the scream and walk toward the source. Example: 20 affects just the nearby street; 80–100 can wake up half the neighborhood. Very high values make every scream a mini-horde event.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ChaseCooldownHours_too: Minimum in-game hours between screams from the SAME sprinter during a chase. 0.01 ≈ about 36 in-game seconds. Higher values make chases quieter; lower ones make them louder and more frantic.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ChaseScreechChance_too: Extra chance for a scream while the sprinter is already chasing you. Use low values (5–20) for occasional screams and higher ones for chaotic, noisy pursuits. Combine this with the cooldown setting to avoid endless screaming.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ClusterCooldownHours_t: Duration of the time window controlling screams per group (cluster), in in-game hours. Within this window, the total number of screams is limited by 'Max screams per group'. Example: 0.01 ≈ about 36 in-game seconds for that area.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ClusterRadius_tooltip: Defines the size of the area considered a single screaming scene. If multiple sprinters are within this radius, they count as one group (cluster). The scream limit per group applies to all of them, preventing endless chaos in crowded areas.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_EnableNearScream_toolt: When enabled, the sprinter emits an extra scream when entering close range (face scream), in addition to the discovery and chase screams. Disabling it reduces audio chaos in melee combat and keeps the mod cleaner in dense hordes.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_FarRange_tooltip: Maximum distance in tiles at which the discovery scream can be heard in 3D. Higher values make the sound travel farther, warning you of sprinters before you see them. Useful in open maps where echoes enhance immersion.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_FarVolume_tooltip: Controls the volume of the discovery scream when the sprinter is still far away. Example: 0.1 gives a faint echo; values near 1.0 make the scream stand out even from a distance.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_GlobalVolume_tooltip: General volume multiplier applied to all screams in the mod. 1.0 = default; 0.5 = half volume; 2.0 = double volume (careful with your ears). Use this to balance the mod’s audio with the rest of the game.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxClusterScreams_tool: Maximum number of screams allowed in each group during the set window. Example: with value 2, even if 10 sprinters spot you at once, only 2 screams will be heard in that scene.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxProcessDistance_too: Maximum distance in tiles from the player within which theySEE YOU still processes sprinters for screams. Zombies beyond this radius are ignored to save performance. Values between 180 and 250 maintain immersion while staying efficient.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_MaxScreamsPerChapter_t: Scream limit for each chapter of a hunt. A chapter resets when the sprinter loses you and finds you again, so long chases stay alive instead of going permanently silent (v1.0 behavior). Example: 4 allows discovery + face scream + two chase screams per chapter.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_NearAsWorldSound_toolt: If enabled, the close scream uses PlayWorldSound just like the distant one — full 3D sound with spatial direction and echo, perfect for headsets. If disabled, it uses the zombie’s local audio, sharper and more direct. (v1.1: deprecated — the close scream now always plays in 3D from the zombie itself.)
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_NearVolume_tooltip: Volume multiplier when the sprinter screams right in your face. For a stronger jump scare, use 1.0 or higher; high values make screams much more aggressive.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_PitchVariation_tooltip: Each sprinter rolls a personal voice pitch within this range and keeps it for life, so the same voice bank produces thousands of distinct hunters. 0 disables it (all voices identical); 7 gives clearly distinct voices while staying natural.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_RediscoveryHours_toolt: How long (in in-game hours) a sprinter must lose sight of you before its discovery scream re-arms. When it spots you again, a new hunt chapter begins — expect a fresh 'FOUND YOU' scream. 0.04 = a few real seconds; higher values make rediscoveries rarer and more dramatic.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ScreechChance_tooltip: Probability that a sprinter will let out a discovery scream the first time they see you. 0 = never screams; 100 = almost every sprinter screams as soon as they spot you. Example: 60 means roughly 6 out of 10 encounters start with a scream. (v1.1: DEPRECATED — the identification scream is now ALWAYS guaranteed, on first sight and on every re-sight. This option has no effect anymore.)
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ShoutResponseRadius_to: Maximum distance at which a sprinter can hear and answer your shout. 50 covers the surrounding streets; higher values let the whole neighborhood answer.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_ShoutResponse_tooltip: When you shout, up to two nearby sprinters scream back after a short beat — call and response. They reveal their position and voice before you ever see them.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_TickRate_tooltip: How many ticks the game waits before reprocessing each sprinter. Lower values = faster reaction but more CPU load; higher = lighter but slower. 6 is a recommended balance for large hordes and helicopter events.
Sandbox_SIMBA_TSY_TimeMode_tooltip: Defines at what time of day sprinters can use their special scream. 0 = day and night; 1 = day only; 2 = night only. Example: use '2' for calmer days and much more tense nights.

Sandbox_zReV2_AntibodyPower2_tooltip:
Affects how quickly resistant antibodies eliminate the zombie virus from the body after activation in the stage.
-This trait is acquired by injecting the level 4 vaccine;
-If potency = 6, then ~5% infection is removed per hour;
-If potency = 12, then ~10% infection is removed per hour;
-If potency = 24, then ~20% infection is removed per hour.
Sandbox_zReV2_AntibodyPower_tooltip:
Affects at which infection stage the resistant antibodies activate.
-This trait is acquired by injecting the level 4 vaccine;
-TERMINAL - when infected over 80%, health drains, high chance of death;
-PRETERMINAL - when infected over 60% (nausea, fever)(RECOMMENDED!);
-MODERATE - when infected over 40% (mild nausea);
-INITIAL - when infected over 20% (no symptoms).
Sandbox_zReV2_BookInWorldSpawnChance_too:
Affects the number of laboratory (mod) books in the world.
-Setting to 0 disables their world spawn;
-Does not affect book drops from special zombies.
Sandbox_zReV2_DefaultVaccineSpawnChance_:
First-level vaccine that reduces infection to 5%.
-This option affects the drop chance in SPECIAL ZOMBIES.
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchMinHealthNotificat:
Affects at what health level the character will notify
about crossing the critical health threshold specified in this parameter!
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchRand_tooltip:
Only works for the vaccine improvement research type "PROGRESSIVE CHANCE" and "FULL RESEARCH"!
-In case of failed research, increases the result by a randomizer depending on this number (hereafter referred to as X);
-The formula works as:
Rand(X, X*2) for research up to level 2;
Rand(X*0.75, X*1.5) for research up to level 3;
Rand(X*0.5, X) for research up to level 4!
-Rounded up to the nearest whole number;
-Simply put: the randomizer decreases for researching a new vaccine by ~30% on average.
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchReduceHealth_toolt: When performing the recipe "Take blood for further work" your health will be reduced by this value!
Sandbox_zReV2_ResearchType_tooltip:
Choice of result type for improving (researching) new vaccine levels.
-PROGRESSIVE CHANCE - on failure, the next success chance increases (accumulates);
-STATIC CHANCE - fixed percentage chance of success (30,20,14% from second to fourth);
-FULL RESEARCH - there is a hidden progress bar for study (100 units, conditionally, each research fills the bar).
